instructions.value: Participants were instructed to work to earn the beverage cued by the label by making fast, correct joystick responses: pull the joystick toward the body for approach trials and push it away from the body for avoid trials. Responses had to be made within an adaptive deadline.

spans.text: In order to earn the reward cued by the label, participants had to follow the response instructions, i.e., approach (pull towards their body) or avoid (push away from their body).

stimuli.value: Reward cues consisting of neutral, low-calorie, or high-calorie beverage labels, followed after a jittered 2–6 s delay by one of four shape targets indicating an approach or avoid response; feedback and beverage-receipt pictures were also presented.

spans.text: Trials started with a reward cue (i.e., one of the labels: neutral/low-calorie/high-calorie), which predicted the beverage reward for correct performance.
RTs and accuracy were analyzed with mixed-level models

caption.value: Behavioral results. RTs (in milliseconds) and error rates (in percentages) for each combination of reward cue label and instructed movement.
